title: How to Form a Wyoming LLC for Non-US Residents
summary: A complete guide to forming a Wyoming LLC for non-US residents, including costs, requirements, and compliance. Learn how to get started today.
body_markdown:
Wyoming is a premier destination for international entrepreneurs seeking tax advantages, robust asset protection, and minimal administrative friction.


Whether you sell on Amazon, consult globally, or manage an investment portfolio, the core structure remains the same: a **Wyoming LLC for non-US residents** . It gives foreign founders a legal foothold in the US market without requiring physical relocation or citizenship.


Setting up a US entity from abroad may seem daunting, but[Wyoming makes it remarkably simple](https://www.doola.com/llc/wyoming/) . There is no requirement to live in Wyoming, or anywhere in the US to own and operate your business.


**What You’ll Learn in This Guide**


- **Core Benefits:** Why top global founders choose Wyoming for privacy and tax efficiency.


- **Transparent Costs:** An itemized breakdown of state fees and ongoing maintenance costs.


- **Legal Requirements:** Essential compliance steps for foreign owners.


- **2026 Compliance Updates:** The streamlined filing changes that removed redundant reporting steps for foreign-owned LLCs.


- **Streamlined Setup:** How doola handles every step to make your US entry seamless.


## Benefits of a Wyoming LLC for Non-US Residents


A Wyoming LLC for non-US residents comes with a specific set of advantages worth knowing before filing anything.


**✔ No State Income Tax:** Wyoming[does not impose a state income tax](https://www.doola.com/blog/wyoming-llc-taxation-for-non-us-residents/) on LLCs. This means more profits stay in your pocket.


**✔ Strong Asset Protection:** Wyoming’s laws protect LLC owners from personal liability, making it an ideal choice for entrepreneurs who want to safeguard their assets.


**✔ 100% Foreign Ownership Allowed:** You don’t need to be a US citizen or resident to start a Wyoming LLC.


**✔ No Annual Reports for Single-Member LLCs:** If you’re the sole owner of your Wyoming LLC, you don’t need to file an annual report, reducing paperwork.


**✔ Privacy & Anonymity:** Wyoming does not require LLC owners to be publicly listed, offering a high level of privacy.

## Can a Foreigner Start a Wyoming LLC?


Yes. Wyoming’s LLC statute doesn’t require US citizenship or residency to form or own an LLC, and there’s no nationality restriction of any kind.


That makes a Wyoming LLC for non-US residents a workable option for international entrepreneurs who want access to the US market without relocating.


**Do I have to live in Wyoming to start an LLC?**


No. Ownership and formation don’t require living in Wyoming, or the US at all. A Wyoming-based registered agent satisfies the physical-address requirement instead.


**Can I open an LLC in Wyoming without living there or being a US citizen?**


Yes. Citizenship status and physical presence are separate from LLC ownership under Wyoming law. Filing the Articles of Organization doesn’t involve any immigration or residency check, and Wyoming doesn’t require a Social Security Number to form the LLC.


**What’s required?**


✔ A Registered Agent (a US-based service to receive legal documents).


✔ An EIN (Employer Identification Number) from the IRS (needed to open a US bank account).


✔ A US mailing address (not mandatory, but useful for business operations).


### A Quick Note on “Foreign LLC” Terminology


Wyoming’s own paperwork uses the term “foreign LLC” differently than most non-US founders expect.


In Wyoming statute, a foreign LLC is a business already formed in another US state, or another country, that’s registering to do business in Wyoming. That’s filed through a Certificate of Authority, at a $150 filing fee, and it’s a separate process from forming a Wyoming LLC for non-US residents from scratch, which is what this guide covers.


Anyone who already owns an LLC elsewhere and wants to register it in Wyoming should look up Wyoming’s foreign LLC registration process specifically, rather than following the formation steps below.


## Wyoming Foreign LLC Registration Requirements


- To complete Wyoming foreign LLC registration, the LLC must already be legally formed in another state or jurisdiction.


- Appoint a Wyoming registered agent with a physical street address in the state.


- Complete and file the Application for Certificate of Authority with the Wyoming Secretary of State.


- Provide an original Certificate of Existence/Good Standing from the LLC’s home state, generally issued within 60 days of filing.


- Pay the $150 foreign LLC registration filing fee.


- Ensure the LLC name is available and complies with Wyoming naming requirements; an alternate name may be required if the existing name is unavailable.


- After registration, maintain ongoing Wyoming compliance, including filing the annual report and paying the applicable annual license tax.


## Step-By-Step Guide to Forming a Wyoming LLC for Non-US Residents


Forming a Wyoming LLC for non-US residents follows the same eight steps as it does for anyone else. None of them require a US address of the founder’s own, a Social Security Number, or a trip to Wyoming.


**What to Know Before You Register a Foreign Wyoming LLC**


Before you **register a foreign Wyoming LLC** ,keep these key filing, compliance, and cost requirements in mind:


Every foreign LLC must continuously maintain a **registered agent with a physical street address in Wyoming** . A PO box, virtual address, mail-forwarding location, UPS store, or FedEx store alone does not qualify.


If the LLC’s existing name isn’t available in Wyoming, it must submit a **Use of Fictitious Name** form with its Certificate of Authority application.


Wyoming foreign LLCs must file an **annual report** . The annual license tax is **$60 minimum or 0.0002 of assets located and employed in Wyoming, whichever is greater** .


A business that transacts business in Wyoming without obtaining authority can face a **$5,000 penalty** , plus applicable fees and license taxes, **18% interest** , and potentially audit and attorney costs.


Not every activity triggers foreign registration. Wyoming specifically lists activities such as **maintaining a bank account, selling through independent contractors, and certain isolated transactions completed within 30 days** among activities that, by themselves, do not constitute transacting business.


There are a few steps that trip up non-resident founders specifically, covered one by one below.


### Step 1: Choose a Unique Name for Your Wyoming LLC


Your LLC name needs to be unique and compliant with Wyoming’s naming rules. The Wyoming Secretary of State (SOS) won’t approve your LLC if another business already has that name. So, before you fall in love with “Global Ventures LLC,” make sure it’s available.


**How to check if your desired LLC name is available:**


- Visit the[Wyoming Secretary of State Business Name Search](https://www.google.com/search?client=safari&rls=en&q=Wyoming+Secretary+of+State+Business+Name+Search&ie=UTF-8&oe=UTF-8) and run a quick search.


- The name must include “LLC” or “Limited Liability Company.”


- It cannot include words like “bank,” “insurance,” or “university” unless you meet additional licensing requirements.


**Pro Tip:** If you’re set on a name but aren’t ready to file, Wyoming allows you to reserve the name for 120 days by filing a Name Reservation Request ($60 fee).


### Step 2: Appoint a Wyoming Registered Agent


A registered agent is a person or company that receives legal documents, tax notices, and government mail for your LLC. Since you’re outside the US, you must have one in Wyoming.


**Requirements for a registered agent:**


- Must be a Wyoming resident or a company with a physical address in Wyoming.


- P.O. boxes aren’t allowed. You need a real street address.


- Must be available during normal business hours (9 AM – 5 PM MST) to receive official documents.

### Step 3: File the Wyoming LLC Articles of Organization


This is the official document that legally forms your LLC with the Wyoming Secretary of State.


**What information do you need?**


- Your LLC name


- Registered agent’s name and address


- Mailing and principal office address (can be the same)


- Organizer’s name (you or the service filing on your behalf)


**Processing time:** Wyoming is fast. It typically takes 1-3 business days for online filings and about two weeks for mail filings.


How doola helps? We prepare and file the Articles of Organization on your behalf, ensuring everything is correct so you don’t face unnecessary delays.


### Step 4: Get an EIN (Employer Identification Number) from the IRS


An EIN is a unique number assigned by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) to identify your business for tax purposes. You’ll need it to:


- Open a US business bank account


- Hire employees (if applicable)


- File US taxes (if required for your business)


If you don’t have a Social Security Number (SSN) or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN), you’ll have to apply for an EIN manually by[filling out IRS Form SS-4](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-4562) and faxing or mailing it to the IRS. The online application is only available for US citizens and residents.


Processing times for an EIN application vary, but it can take anywhere from four to six weeks when applying from outside the US.

### Step 5: Open a US Business Bank Account


[A US business bank account](https://www.doola.com/go-mercury/) makes financial transactions easier, allowing you to receive payments from US customers and vendors without high international fees.


Some banks require an in-person visit, while others, like Relay, allow remote applications for non-US residents.


To open a bank account, you’ll need:


- Your Wyoming LLC formation documents


- Your EIN from the IRS


- A copy of your passport or government-issued ID


- An Operating Agreement (some banks require this)


doola partners with US banks that accept international business owners, making it easier for you to set up an account without traveling to the US.


### Step 6: Create an Operating Agreement (Highly Recommended)


Although Wyoming does not legally require an Operating Agreement, having one is beneficial.


This document outlines ownership details, profit-sharing arrangements, and how decisions are made within the company. It helps prevent disputes between owners and adds credibility when dealing with banks or potential investors.


doola provides a[customized Operating Agreement](https://www.doola.com/pricing/) for your Wyoming LLC as part of the formation package.


### Step 7: Stay Compliant with Wyoming LLC Annual Filings


Once your Wyoming LLC is formed, you need to keep it compliant by filing an Annual Report. This report confirms your business details and ensures your LLC remains in good standing with the state.


- The Annual Report is due each year on the first day of your LLC’s formation month


- The filing fee starts at $60, depending on your business assets in Wyoming


Forgetting to file your Annual Report can result in penalties or even the dissolution of your LLC. doola tracks your deadlines and files your annual reports, ensuring compliance throughout.


### Step 8: Pay Your Taxes (If Applicable)


Wyoming has no state income tax, making it one of the most tax-friendly states for business owners.


However, if the business earns income in the US, federal taxes may still need to be filed with the IRS, depending on US-based income, US employees or physical operations, and any applicable tax treaties.


[Foreign LLC owners typically file Form 5472](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f5472--2012.pdf) along with a pro forma Form 1120, and this applies every year the LLC exists, even in a year with zero income or activity.


Missing the deadline or leaving out a reportable transaction can trigger a **$25,000 penalty per form, per year** . The penalty can increase by another $25,000 for every 30 days an IRS notice goes unanswered, even if the LLC made no profit.


**Given the penalty exposure, this isn’t a form to guess on.**


[doola’s tax and bookkeeping team](https://www.doola.com/bookkeeping/) handles Form 5472 and pro forma 1120 filings for foreign-owned LLCs, so the deadline gets met correctly every year, whether the business had activity or not.


## Do Non-US Residents Owe US Tax on LLC Income at All?


It depends on where the work happens, not just where the LLC is formed. The IRS splits a non-resident owner’s income into two buckets.


[Effectively Connected Income (ECI)](https://irs.gov/individuals/international-taxpayers/effectively-connected-income-eci) applies when the LLC is actually engaged in a US trade or business, such as having a US office, US employees, or US inventory, and it’s taxed at graduated federal rates from 10% to 37%, the same brackets a US resident pays,[reported on Form 1040-NR](https://www.doola.com/blog/what-is-irs-form-1040-and-what-do-i-do-with-it/) .


Fixed, Determinable, Annual, or Periodic income (FDAP), on the other hand, covers passive US-source payments like dividends, royalties, or interest, and it’s taxed at a flat 30% (or a lower rate under a tax treaty, if one applies and the correct paperwork, usually Form W-8BEN, has been filed).


A non-resident running an online business through a Wyoming LLC with no US office, no US employees, and no one in the US regularly signing contracts on their behalf is often not engaged in a US trade or business at all, which means no ECI and potentially no US federal income tax owed on that income.


[That same owner would still face 30% withholding](https://irs.gov/individuals/international-taxpayers/taxation-of-nonresident-aliens) (or a treaty-reduced rate) on any US-source dividends, royalties, or interest paid to them, and the Form 5472 filing obligation applies regardless of which bucket the income falls into.


None of this is a substitute for a tax professional’s review of the specific facts, but knowing the distinction upfront helps a founder ask the right questions instead of assuming either “fully tax-free” or “fully taxable.”


#### A Note on Wyoming’s Foreign-Ownership Law


Wyoming House Bill 69, effective July 1, 2025, gave the Secretary of State authority to administratively dissolve a corporation or LLC found to be[owned or controlled by a “foreign adversary,”](https://wyoleg.gov/2025/SessionLaws.pdf) a narrow, federally-defined list maintained by the US Secretary of Commerce, not a general restriction on non-US ownership.


In practice, this targets entities tied to countries the federal government has specifically designated as adversarial, and it does not affect the vast majority of non-resident founders forming a Wyoming LLC from the UK, EU, India, Canada, or elsewhere. It’s worth knowing the law exists, mainly so a founder isn’t caught off guard by references to it elsewhere.


## Do Non-US Residents Still Need to File a BOI Report?


As of August 14, 2026, no, not for a Wyoming LLC for non-US residents. FinCEN’s final rule permanently exempts every entity formed in the United States, including a Wyoming LLC owned entirely by a non-US resident, from Beneficial Ownership Information reporting under the Corporate Transparency Act.


The exemption covers the LLC and its owners, regardless of where those owners live. Only entities formed under foreign law that register to do business in the US still have to report, and only for their non-US-person beneficial owners. It’s a recent change,[confirmed directly through FinCEN](https://fincen.gov/boi) , and it removes a compliance step that used to apply to foreign-owned Wyoming LLCs.

## Can You Run a Wyoming LLC Remotely?


Running a Wyoming LLC out of state, or out of the country entirely, is the norm for non-resident owners, not the exception. And one of the biggest advantages of forming a Wyoming LLC is that you don’t need to be physically present in the US to run it.


Whether you’re an entrepreneur working from another country or simply don’t need a physical office, Wyoming’s business-friendly laws make remote management easy.


##### 1. Running an LLC Without a US Office or Employees


Wyoming LLCs do not require a US office or local employees. This means you can run your business from anywhere using digital tools, automation, and outsourcing.


Instead of hiring full-time US employees, many Wyoming LLC owners outsource tasks to freelancers, contractors, or virtual assistants globally.[Platforms like Fiverr](https://www.doola.com/go-fiverr/) , make it easy to build a remote workforce.


And, if you need a US-based phone number for customer service or credibility, VoIP services like Google Voice, OpenPhone, or RingCentral can provide a professional number that works globally.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid When Setting Up a Wyoming LLC as a Non-Resident


Forming a Wyoming LLC as a foreigner is one of the easiest ways to enter the US market. But only if you do it right.


Here are the pitfalls that trip up non-residents (and how to avoid them):


**🚫 Skipping a Registered Agent –** Wyoming requires you to have a registered agent with a physical address in the state. No address = No LLC. Plus, without any physical address, you won’t receive critical legal or tax notices.


**🚫 Not Having a US Business Address –** Many banks and payment processors reject applications without a proper US business address. A virtual mailbox or forwarding service keeps your LLC compliant and operational.


**🚫 Forgetting to Apply for an EIN –** No Employer Identification Number (EIN) means no US business bank account and no way to file taxes properly. The IRS provides EINs for free, but the process can be tricky for non-residents. You can take doola’s help if you need clear guidance on obtaining your EIN number.


**🚫 Picking the Wrong Bank –** Not all US banks accept foreign-owned LLCs. Choose Wyoming-friendly banking with Mercury or Relay as a non-resident. **Note:** Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.


**🚫 Ignoring Tax Responsibilities –** Wyoming has no state income tax, but that doesn’t mean you’re tax-free. Depending on where your customers are,[sales tax](https://www.doola.com/products/sales-tax-and-reseller-certificate/) , federal tax, and local taxes may still apply. And, missing a filing, could lead to fines or compliance issues.


**🚫 Mixing Personal & Business Finances –** Using your personal bank account for business transactions can jeopardize liability protection. A dedicated business account and proper bookkeeping keep you in the clear.


**🚫 Choosing the Wrong LLC Structure –** A Single-Member LLC vs. Multi-Member LLC affects taxes, liability, and banking. Make sure you pick the right setup from the start.

### What doola’s Formation Team Hears During 1:1 Consultations


Beyond the standard questions, these are the ones that come up most often once a non-resident founder gets on a call to actually form a Wyoming LLC.


#### **“Will forming the LLC automatically get me a US bank account?”**


No. The LLC and the bank account are two separate steps. Formation happens first, then the EIN, then the bank application. Some banks approve non-resident applicants remotely, others want a video call, and approval isn’t guaranteed just because the LLC exists.


#### **“Can I use my home country address as the LLC’s official address?”**


The registered agent’s Wyoming address is what’s required on the state filing. A home country address can still be used for the owner’s own contact and mailing purposes, but it doesn’t substitute for the registered agent requirement.


#### **“Now that BOI reporting doesn’t apply to me, does the IRS still know who owns the LLC?”**


Yes, separately. The BOI exemption only removes the FinCEN filing. The IRS still gets ownership information through the EIN application and, where applicable, Form 5472. The two systems aren’t connected.


#### **“If my registered agent quits or the service lapses, what happens to my LLC while I’m overseas?”**


Wyoming allows a grace period to name a replacement agent, but missing it risks administrative dissolution. This is one of the more common panic calls doola’s team gets, and it’s avoidable by keeping registered agent service active and billing current.


#### **“Can I add a US-based co-founder to the LLC later?”**


Yes. A Wyoming LLC’s membership can change after formation through an amendment and an updated operating agreement. It doesn’t require dissolving and re-forming the LLC.


## FAQs


#### **Can I own a Wyoming LLC if I don’t live in the US?**


Yes, non-US residents can fully own and operate a Wyoming LLC without needing US citizenship or residency.


#### **Do I need a US address to form a Wyoming LLC?**


No, but a registered agent with a physical address in Wyoming is required, which doola provides.


#### **How do I pay taxes as a foreign LLC owner?**


Tax obligations depend on how the LLC operates. With no US-based income, US taxes may not be owed, but a tax professional can confirm.


#### **Can a Wyoming LLC help me get a US visa or residency?**


No, forming an LLC does not automatically grant a visa or residency. An investor or business visa may be needed, depending on the situation.


#### **How do I dissolve my Wyoming LLC if I no longer need it?**


Articles of Dissolution must be filed with the Wyoming Secretary of State, with all taxes and liabilities settled before closing the LLC.


#### **Can I run my Wyoming US LLC out of state?**


Yes. Beyond the registered agent’s Wyoming address, there’s no requirement to operate, bank, or live in Wyoming, or anywhere in the US, to keep the LLC in good standing.


#### **Is a Wyoming LLC still considered a Wyoming US LLC if a non-resident owns it?**


Yes. Ownership by a non-US resident doesn’t change its legal status. It’s formed under Wyoming law and treated as a US LLC for banking, contracts, and federal tax purposes where applicable.


#### **What’s the process for setting up a Wyoming LLC for non-US residents?**


It follows the same eight steps as any Wyoming LLC: choosing a name, appointing a registered agent, filing the Articles of Organization, getting an EIN, opening a US bank account, drafting an operating agreement, and staying current on annual filings. None of the steps require living in the US.
